Ajnabee released on 21 September 2001. Twenty-five years today.

Abbas–Mustan's Switzerland-set thriller: two couples, an insurance plot and a murder charge. Akshay Kumar won Best Villain at the Filmfare Awards for it.
Bipasha Basu made her debut and won Best Female Debut.
It opened on Kareena Kapoor's 21st birthday, in her second year in films.
And it was an unofficial remake of the 1992 American thriller Consenting Adults.

Still know every Anu Malik track from it?

Diwali just got crowded.

Suriya's next is titled Scene, and it opens on 6 November — the same day as Ramayana: Part 1.
He plays a chain-smoking cop credited with 900 arrests. Jithu Madhavan (Romancham, Aavesham) directs his first Tamil film; Sushin Shyam scores; Nazriya Nazim and Naslen co-star.
Ramayana, meanwhile, has Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, with a score by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer.
Diwali falls on 8 November. Both films are betting on the two days before it.

Meghna Gulzar's Daayra is dividing critics.

Kareena Kapoor Khan plays DCP Ajooni Kohli; Prithviraj Sukumaran plays DCP Raman Kumar. Two officers, one case, two very different readings of duty and the law.
Gulzar has said the team looked at several real cases while writing it, rather than one.
Reviews praise the performances and the moral complexity; several flag the pacing. It released on 18 September.

Why have you not seen Manjummel Boys?

A group of friends from Kochi visits the Guna Caves in Kodaikanal. One of them falls into a 120-foot chasm. It really happened, in 2006.
Soubin Shahir leads; Chidambaram directs.
It grossed about ₹242 crore worldwide — the first Malayalam film past ₹200 crore — and won 10 awards at the Kerala State Film Awards.

text:
A Naga film just won in Toronto.

Theja Rio's debut feature Angh won the Platform Prize at TIFF 2026 on Sunday. It was the only Indian film in the Platform competition, up against 11 others.
Set in 1960s Nagaland, it follows a Konyak chief and his son as an American missionary arrives and their world starts to change.
The jury praised its "vision, audacity and courage".

Add it to the list of films you'll pretend you saw at a festival.

Khosla Ka Ghosla released 20 years ago today.

22 September 2006. Anupam Kher's Kamal Kishore Khosla buys a plot in Delhi and Boman Irani's builder grabs it. The family gets it back the only way left: a con.
Made for ₹3.75 crore in 45 Delhi days. Investors wanted action scenes and an item song. The team said no, and their first backer walked.
Dibakar Banerjee's debut, written by Jaideep Sahni. It won the National Award for Best Hindi Film.

Still the best property-dispute film ever made?

Dor released 20 years ago today, and it's still a hidden gem.

Nagesh Kukunoor, 22 September 2006. Gul Panag's Zeenat has one way to save her husband from execution abroad: the victim's widow has to forgive him.
Ayesha Takia plays that widow, Meera, stuck in a Rajasthani household that has stopped letting her live. Shreyas Talpade is the shape-shifting bahurupiya who helps Zeenat find her.
Two women, one decision, and nobody you can easily hate.

It's a remake of the Malayalam film Perumazhakkalam (2004).

text:
Drishyam: The Conclusion opens on 2 October. Here's the story so far.

2013: Jeethu Joseph's Malayalam original, with Mohanlal as Georgekutty.
2015: the Hindi remake. Ajay Devgn is Vijay Salgaonkar and Tabu plays IG Meera Deshmukh.
2021/2022: Drishyam 2, first in Malayalam straight to Prime Video, then in Hindi.
May 2026: Drishyam 3 grosses ₹237.7 crore, the franchise's biggest film.
2 Oct: The Conclusion. Director Abhishek Pathak says the new title is there to make clear this story ends.

Malayalam or Hindi first?

Maharaja 2 is confirmed, so here's your homework.

A Chennai barber reports a stolen dustbin. The police suspect it isn't really about the dustbin.
Vijay Sethupathi leads, Anurag Kashyap co-stars, and Nithilan Saminathan's timeline does the rest. Go in knowing nothing.
It released in China in November 2024 on more than 40,000 screens and became the biggest Indian film there since the pandemic.

Mind-bender. Streaming on Netflix.
